Subject: Inventory-driven refresh plan: MDM + EDR + VulnStack (ops handbook draft)

Team —

Per our Q3 tooling review, the current MDM (MobileGuard), EDR (SentinelEdge), and our Vuln scanner (VulnStack) renewals converge over the next 90 days. I want to propose an "inventory-driven refresh" approach: we consolidate licensing under a single renewal with staggered rollout windows tied to our device inventory and risk tiering.

High-level ask:
- Vendor to provide a consolidated renewal quote (single contract + SOW) with line items for MDM, EDR, Vuln scanning.
- Pricing options: 12-mo vs 24-mo, commitment discounts, and a staged deployment credit if we defer licenses for low-risk endpoints.
- SOW should include a patch and agent rollout plan (windows, test cohort, rollback).

Why this approach:
- We can reduce overlap on overlapping AV/EDR features and avoid double-agent churn.
- Inventory-driven staging keeps high-risk servers prioritized while deferring low-risk dev machines to a later wave.

Marissa — can you draft the ops handbook appendix for staging criteria (risk tiers, OS filter, owner communications)?
Dev — can you validate that our MDM policy automation supports staggered agent enforcement?
Samir — can you provide consolidated pricing and a sample SOW by Monday (8/30)?

I attached the inventory export and a one-page cost target. I expect this to feed the procurement PO request next week.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Platform Security
Redwood Inference
